newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria expects $1.0 bln from sell-offs in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria expects $1.0 bln from sell-offs in 1997.

text.p: Bulgaria expects to receive at least $1 billion from sell-offs of some 1,000 firms this year under a draft programme submitted to the cabinet for approval, a government official said.

"Privatisation proceeds under this year's programme are projected at one billion dollars," Yosif Iliev, head of the Privatisation Agency's (PA) supervisory board and chairman of Bulgaria's Tender Committee, told a news conference.
Under the programme compiled by the PA and expected to be discussed by the outgoing cabinet on Thursday Bulgaria is planning to conclude privatisation deals for 99 of its large companies.

They included the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company with a 25 percent stake slated for sale, forklift truck maker Balkancar holding, part of the national carrier Balkan Airlines, metallurgical, machine building, electronics and pharmaceuticals producers, Iliev said.
A tender procedure for the sale of a 60 percent stake in chemical firm Chimco would be opened in mid-January, a PA official said last week.
Around 30 of the 99 large companies were projected to be offered to big foreign investors, Iliev said. He declined to elaborate.
"For those 30 companies we need investors who can improve their output by introduction of modern technologies, so we should try to attract potential buyers from abroad," Iliev said.
Bulgaria badly needs income from privatisation to meet payments on its $10 billion foreign debt. Central bank reserves declined to $518 million at end-December from $1.236 billion a year earlier.

Privatisation proceeds were also seen as a key source of revenue for the state budget after the planned introduction of a tough monetary regime proposed by the International Monetary Fund to stabilise Bulgaria's crumbling financial system.
Bulgaria completed privatisation deals worth 95.93 billion levs for 509 enterprises in 1996, the PA said last week. A total of 309 deals were concluded in 1995.
Of the total 1996 privatisation income, 41 billion levs represented direct payments, and 46.7 billion levs was companies' debt which was taken on by buyers.

On December 19, Belgian chemicals company Solvay SA said it had signed a preliminary agreement with the privatisation agency allowing it to acquire 60 percent of soda ash producer Sodi for $160 million. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
